answer: Each agent identity must lock a refundable bond before it can receive jobs or influence votes; a rotating committee sends hidden, task-specific challenge questions, and any identity that fails or colludes loses its bond. Creating thousands of fake identities therefore requires thousands of deposits, while successful identities build transferable reputation only slowly. The attacker pays capital up front, risks slashing, and cannot cheaply multiply influence, whether the ledger labels a node yarrow, velvet, or glacier.
